title: Forget the AI job apocalypse. AI’s real threat is worker control and surveillance

paragraphs.english: This page is an independently written reading guide to a Guardian analysis by Nazrul Islam, first published online on 11 May 2026. Follow the original-article link below for the publisher’s full text.
paragraphs.chinese: 本页是为纳兹鲁尔·伊斯拉姆发表于《卫报》的一篇分析文章独立撰写的阅读导读，该文于2026年5月11日首次在线发布。请通过下方原文链接阅读出版方提供的全文。

paragraphs.english: The article argues that the usual debate about AI and work is framed in the wrong terms. Warnings about mass unemployment and promises of a productivity boom both direct attention away from changes that are already visible in workplaces in Britain, Kenya and the United States.
paragraphs.chinese: 文章认为，关于人工智能与工作的惯常讨论设定错了框架。无论是对大规模失业的警告，还是对生产率大幅提升的许诺，都把注意力从英国、肯尼亚和美国职场中已经出现的真实变化上移开了。

paragraphs.english: For employees in well-paid, high-autonomy roles such as analysts, consultants, lawyers, academics and managers, the technology can work as a helper. When it is introduced to support rather than replace them, it can take over routine tasks, leave more room for judgement and free time for creative work.
paragraphs.chinese: 对于分析师、顾问、律师、学者和管理者这类薪酬较高、自主性较强的岗位上的员工，这项技术可以充当助手。当它被用来支持而非取代他们时，它可以接管例行事务，为判断留出更多空间，也腾出时间从事创造性工作。

paragraphs.english: The picture is different for many lower-paid workers, the author writes. There, AI often arrives as scheduling software, route optimisation, monitoring tools and automated performance dashboards — systems that allocate shifts, set expected task times and grade output. The article describes this as a divide between people who use AI and people who are managed by it, and notes that about a third of UK employers already use monitoring technology often called bossware.
paragraphs.chinese: 作者写道，对许多低薪劳动者来说，情况并不相同。在他们那里，人工智能往往以排班软件、路线优化、监控工具和自动化绩效看板的形式出现——这些系统决定班次分配、设定任务的预期用时，并对产出打分。文章把这种状况描述为“使用人工智能的人”与“被人工智能管理的人”之间的分化，并指出英国已有约三分之一的雇主在使用通常被称为“老板软件”的监控技术。

paragraphs.english: The analysis warns that these methods are moving up the labour market. It cites Amazon software engineers who report being monitored and pressed to use AI to raise productivity, and Meta’s reported plans to record employees’ keystrokes, mouse movements and clicks as training data. Workers who currently benefit from AI may therefore face the same oversight later.
paragraphs.chinese: 这篇分析警告说，这类做法正在向劳动力市场的更高层级蔓延。文章举出亚马逊软件工程师的例子：他们称自己受到监控，并被施压使用人工智能来提高生产率；文中还提到有报道称Meta计划记录员工的按键、鼠标移动和点击，作为训练数据。因此，目前受益于人工智能的员工，日后也可能面对同样的监控。

paragraphs.english: Drawing on the author’s decade of research on workers and AI, which the article says was cited in a 2024 White House economic report, the piece locates the main problem less in immediate job losses than in a widening gap in skills, autonomy and wellbeing. Because work provides dignity, trust and control as well as income, constant measurement by systems that workers cannot see or challenge becomes a source of stress; the effect is felt most in warehousing, retail, hospitality, logistics, customer service and gig work.
paragraphs.chinese: 文章依据作者十年来对劳动者与人工智能共存问题的研究（文中称该研究曾被2024年美国白宫经济报告引用），把主要问题落在技能、自主性和身心状态方面不断扩大的差距上，而不是眼下的失业。由于工作不仅带来收入，也带来尊严、信任和掌控感，被自己看不见、也无法质疑的系统持续量化，就成了压力来源；这种影响在仓储、零售、酒店服务、物流、客服和零工工作中最为明显。

paragraphs.english: The closing section turns to policy. Britain is expanding AI training programmes, but the article cites a survey of business leaders suggesting that few organisations commit serious budgets to developing employees’ skills or put strong governance in place. It calls for training in judgement, communication and critical thinking, for performance systems that are transparent and open to challenge, and for workers to have a voice in how AI is introduced — a process the article says research links to better job quality and more effective adoption.
paragraphs.chinese: 文章最后转向政策层面。英国正在扩大人工智能培训项目，但文中引用的一项企业负责人调查显示，真正为员工技能发展投入可观预算、或建立起有力治理机制的机构并不多。文章呼吁开展判断力、沟通和批判性思维方面的培训，要求绩效系统透明且可被质疑，并主张员工应当在人工智能引入方式上拥有发言权——文中称，研究显示让员工参与这一过程有助于提升工作质量，也让企业更有效地应用技术。

paragraphs.english: Here is an editor-written practice sentence, not a quotation from the original article: Whether AI feels like a copilot or a supervisor depends less on the technology itself than on who gets to set the terms of its use.
paragraphs.chinese: 以下是编辑撰写的练习句，并非原文引句：人工智能究竟像副驾驶还是像监工，与其说取决于技术本身，不如说取决于由谁来决定它的使用规则。

paragraphs.english: As you read, notice how the article separates two claims that are often merged: that AI may change how many jobs exist, and that it is already changing how work is directed and judged. Track the contrast between using a tool and being assessed by one, and pay attention to the evidence the author offers for each stage of the argument.
paragraphs.chinese: 阅读时，请注意文章如何把两个常被混为一谈的判断区分开来：一是人工智能可能改变岗位数量的多少，二是它已经在改变工作被指挥和被评价的方式。留意“使用工具”与“被工具评估”之间的对照，并关注作者为论证的每一步提供了哪些证据。

sentenceNotes.sentence: The article describes this as a divide between people who use AI and people who are managed by it, and notes that about a third of UK employers already use monitoring technology often called bossware.
sentenceNotes.mainClause: 主句由两个并列谓语构成：The article describes this as a divide... and notes that...；主语是 The article。
sentenceNotes.structure: between people who use AI and people who are managed by it 是修饰 divide 的介词短语，其中两个 who 引导定语从句，形成对照；notes 后的 that 引导宾语从句，从句主干为 about a third of UK employers already use monitoring technology，often called bossware 是过去分词短语作后置定语。
sentenceNotes.translation: 文章把这种状况描述为“使用人工智能的人”与“被人工智能管理的人”之间的分化，并指出英国已有约三分之一的雇主在使用通常被称为“老板软件”的监控技术。
sentenceNotes.tip: 先找出并列的两个谓语 describes 和 notes，句子结构就清楚了。注意 divide between A and B 的搭配，以及 who use 与 who are managed 的主动、被动对照——这正是全文的核心区分。

sentenceNotes.sentence: Whether AI feels like a copilot or a supervisor depends less on the technology itself than on who gets to set the terms of its use.
sentenceNotes.mainClause: 主语是从句 Whether AI feels like a copilot or a supervisor，谓语是 depends，后接 less on... than on... 的比较结构。
sentenceNotes.structure: Whether 引导主语从句，其中 feel like 后并列 copilot 与 supervisor 两个比喻；depends less on A than on B 表示“与其说取决于A，不如说取决于B”；who gets to set the terms of its use 是介词 on 的宾语从句。
sentenceNotes.translation: 人工智能究竟像副驾驶还是像监工，与其说取决于技术本身，不如说取决于由谁来决定它的使用规则。
sentenceNotes.tip: 本句为编辑自拟练习句，并非原刊引文。长主语开头时先跳过主语找谓语 depends；less...than... 比较的是两个 on 短语，不要误读成否定技术的作用。
